entities.summary: Antonio de Viti de Marco was an Italian economist. Born in Lecce, he was professor of public finance in Rome from 1887 until 1931, when he resigned rather than take an oath of loyalty to the Italian fascism regime. He was a longtime editor of the Giornale degli Economisti. He has been described as "an unyielding defender of liberalism". His writings on public goods, taxation, and public debt set the foundation for the modern public choice theory.
